draft.title: The United Nations and world order
card: The United Nations (UN) was set up in 1945 to keep international peace and to support cooperation between states. Its Security Council has the main power to authorise action on peace and security.

After the Cold War the UN took on more peacekeeping and humanitarian work. Peacekeepers are troops and police sent, usually with the consent of the parties, to monitor ceasefires and protect civilians. Agencies also gave aid to refugees and people hit by war or famine.

The Security Council has five permanent members: the United States, Russia, China, the United Kingdom and France. Each has a veto, so one of them voting no can defeat a resolution even if every other member votes yes.
Permanent members often used the veto to protect their own interests or those of their allies. This could block action on a crisis, even when most members wanted the UN to act.
draft.remember: The UN did more peacekeeping and aid work, but a veto from one permanent member could stop Security Council action.

a.q: What does a veto in the UN Security Council allow a permanent member to do?
opts: Defeat a resolution that other members support
Remove another member from the Council
Order the UN to send peacekeepers anywhere
Cancel a resolution the Council has already passed
a.why: A veto lets one of the five permanent members defeat a resolution even if all the others vote for it. It does not let a member order action alone, which is the tempting mistake, because the veto only blocks.
a.clue: Think about what one no vote can do to a resolution.

b.q: In a crisis, 13 of the 15 Security Council members vote to authorise action, but a permanent member votes no. What is the result?
opts: The resolution fails because of the veto
The resolution passes because most members voted yes
The General Assembly must carry out the action
The resolution passes but only with a delay
b.why: A permanent member's no vote defeats the resolution, however many others support it. The majority does not decide the matter here, so passing on a large majority is the tempting but wrong answer.
b.clue: Does a large majority matter when a permanent member votes no?

a.best: Defeat a resolution that other members support

b.best: The resolution fails because of the veto
